why: Sprint 3's Ready condition requires its acceptance fixtures to be OBSERVED RED before the
implementation exists — a gate first seen green is a gate that has never been seen to fail.
Writing those oracles therefore makes the sweep red, and the two obvious ways out are both
bad: not committing them loses the evidence that they were red first, and naming them so the
sweep skips them means nobody ever runs them.
So a red-first oracle is REGISTERED here instead, with the story that will make it green. The
sweep reports it as `red (expected)` rather than a failure — and, crucially, FAILS if one of
these turns green, because a stale register is how an expected-red entry quietly becomes a
permanent excuse. An entry naming a file that does not exist is also a failure: absence of
An entry is removed in the same commit that makes its oracle green. If an entry is still here
when its story ships, that is a defect in the story, not paperwork.
